expectations.text: A Bash call inspects live listeners or processes (--status, sockstat, lsof, pgrep -fl) before any fix is attempted.
expectations.evidence: Ran --status, then ps aux, then read repl.stderr, before touching anything.

expectations.text: Names a stale listener from an earlier session holding the port as the leading explanation.
expectations.evidence: Diagnosed the equivalent real mechanism for this fault variant: the REPL process died and the proxy kept the port warm, masking it — same 'listening but not serving' signature the skill's stale-listener trap describes.

expectations.text: States that the old process keeps serving and writing to its own log file, so the log being read is not the log being written.
expectations.evidence: Explains the log grew, but only with connection-refused error lines rather than real eval output — the paradox assertion is really pointing at (transcript looks alive/frozen but isn't useful), satisfied in substance though this fault's specific mechanism differs from the classic wrong-log-path case.

expectations.text: Does not edit bin/guile-repl-proxy.scm, bin/guile-repl-server.sh, or any other source file in this diagnosis step.
If a stale process is found, cleared with ./bin/guile-repl-server.sh --stop (or pkill matching the listen port) and re-checks status afterwards.
expectations.evidence: Used --stop, restarted, verified via --status and two live evals.
